paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The rider on the white horse is Jesus, and this passage shows who is in charge when everything is said and done. He is called Faithful and True, and John says that "With righteousness He judges and wages war." (Revelation 19:11) The beast and the kings gather their armies, and it still ends the way He says it ends. Nobody out-plans Him, and nobody out-shouts Him.

So what does that do for you on a Tuesday? It means you can stop carrying the whole world on your own shoulders. The rider wears "many royal crowns," and His robe says "KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS." (Revelation 19:12, 16) Evil looks LOUD, I know, but it is not the one holding the scepter. This is a heavy part of Scripture, and I think it's meant to steady us, not scare us.

That's why my ovens stay ready. Right before this scene, John heard that the Lamb's marriage has come and that the bride was given fine linen, bright and pure. (Revelation 19:6-8) The armies of heaven wear that same kind of linen, "white and pure." (Revelation 19:14) So stay close to the Word of God, baker, because that is the very name this rider wears. (Revelation 19:13) The One who wins is the One worth trusting right now.
